package_info.package_versions: all published versions as of April 24th, 2023
package_info.why_malicious: The packages contain heavily obfuscated code that monkey-patches core JavaScript built-ins (sessionStorage.getItem, Array.prototype.includes, Array.prototype.filter, JSON.stringify) to introduce random, non-deterministic, and unpredictable behavior. This undermines the reliability and security of any application that uses them, and the obfuscation is a strong indicator of intent to deceive or hide functionality, a common trait in malicious packages.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At import-time, the code monkey-patches sessionStorage.getItem to randomly (5% probability) reverse the string value returned, introducing unpredictable data retrieval outcomes.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Altering core browser storage APIs to return corrupted or altered data is highly suspicious and can break application logic or mask further malicious activity.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: sessionStorage.getItem is expected to return the exact value stored; introducing random reversals violates this contract.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Rarely, for testing fault tolerance or chaos engineering, but never in production or without clear documentation.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At import-time, the code monkey-patches Array.prototype.includes to always return false for arrays of odd length, causing unpredictable and incorrect inclusion checks.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Modifying fundamental array methods to behave incorrectly undermines application logic and is a classic sabotage technique.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Array.prototype.includes should accurately reflect element presence regardless of array length.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: None in production; only for deliberate chaos testing with clear warnings.
key_indicators: Conditional logic based on array length

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At import-time, the code monkey-patches Array.prototype.filter to randomly (10% probability) remove one element from the result, but only on Sundays, introducing time-based and random data loss.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Introducing random, time-based data loss in a core array method is highly disruptive and can cause subtle, hard-to-debug errors.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Array.prototype.filter should return a deterministic subset based on the filter function, not randomly drop elements.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: None in production; only for chaos engineering with explicit user consent.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At import-time, the code monkey-patches JSON.stringify to randomly (10% probability) replace all uppercase 'I' characters with lowercase 'l' in the output, corrupting serialized data.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Corrupting serialized data output can break APIs, cause data loss, or introduce subtle bugs, especially when done randomly.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: JSON.stringify should produce a faithful, deterministic string representation of the input object.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: None in production; only for deliberate error injection in testing environments.

attack_chain.action: Upon import, the package immediately monkey-patches core JavaScript built-ins (sessionStorage.getItem, Array.prototype.includes, Array.prototype.filter, JSON.stringify) to introduce random, non-deterministic behavior.
attack_chain.leads_to: Any code in the application that relies on these built-ins will behave unpredictably, leading to data corruption, logic errors, and hard-to-debug issues.

behavioral_signatures: Monkey-patching of core JavaScript built-ins at import-time
Introduction of random or probabilistic behavior into standard library functions
Obfuscated code in index.js or main entry point
file_indicators: index.js containing obfuscated or minified code
References to sessionStorage, Array.prototype, or JSON.stringify being reassigned
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Scan for packages that monkey-patch or reassign core JavaScript built-in methods (such as sessionStorage.getItem, Array.prototype.includes/filter, JSON.stringify) in their main entry point, especially if the code is obfuscated or introduces random behavior. Flag any package that alters standard library behavior without clear, documented intent. Automated static analysis can detect assignments to these prototypes or global objects, and code review should be triggered for any obfuscated or minified code in open-source packages.
